sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14:1
items.html:
Explains that there were two restrictions in the worlds. The first restriction was on Malchut alone, and the first nine were clean of any restriction. And in the second restriction, the restriction from Bina downward of every degree was mixed in. And Bina, Tifferet, and Malchut came out of every degree.

The conclusion made in the place of Bina is called Parsa
Now we shall explain the ten Sefirot called the five worlds: Adam Kadmon, Atzilut, Beria, Yetzira, and Assiya. And here one needs to know the two restrictions that were made in the worlds. For at first a restriction was made only in the vessel of Malchut, so that it would not receive into itself the light of Ein Sof. And the first nine Sefirot were clean of any screen and restriction, as written in Part 1. And from this aspect the first three Partzufim in the world of AK extended, called Galgalta, AB, SAG, as explained above in chapter 12. And after this, in this Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, a second restriction was made, in which the Malchut that concludes the line of the light of Ein Sof, which stood at the point of this world, rose to the place of the chest of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, and concluded there the line of the light of Ein Sof, and half of Tifferet and NHY[M] from the chest downward of the Partzuf remained empty without light. And just as a new conclusion was made on the light of the line as a whole, at the place of the chest of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, because of the ascent of Malchut to the Bina of the Guf, called Tifferet, so it was made in particular in the ten Sefirot of every single degree, that the Malchut of that degree rose to the Bina of that degree, and concluded the degree there, and the Bina and TM of that degree went outside the degree, and fell to the degree below it. And this new conclusion that was made in the second restriction, at the place of Bina or Tifferet, is called Parsa.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14:2
items.html:
The general Parsa separates between Atzilut and BYA
And let us speak of the aspect of the general Parsa. That the concluding Malchut that stood at the point of this world rose to the place of the chest of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, and concluded there the light of the line. And this conclusion, made at the place of the chest, is called the general Parsa. And above this Parsa, the world of Atzilut extended. And below this Parsa, namely in the place that was emptied of the light of the line of Ein Sof, the three worlds Beria, Yetzira, Assiya extended, in the secret of the light of offspring. In this way, in the place of half of Tifferet, the world of Beria extended, and in the place of Netzah, Hod, Yesod, the world of Yetzira extended, and in the place of Malchut, the world of Assiya extended. And after special corrections, the world of Beria receives through a screen of phase two from Yeshsut of Atzilut. And the world of Yetzira receives through a screen of phase one from ZA of Atzilut. And the world of Assiya receives through a screen of the root of coarseness, from Malchut of Atzilut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14:3
items.html:
ABYA are the four levels of KHB TM
And therefore the five worlds are considered by the name KHB TM. For the world of AK has the level of Keter, namely the ten Sefirot of Partzuf Galgalta of AK. For every world is considered to have its level according to the first Partzuf in it, just as the level of a set of Sefirot is considered according to the uppermost Sefira in it. And the world of Atzilut has the level of Hochma, namely in the ten Sefirot of Partzuf AA of Atzilut, considered the first Partzuf, since Atik is exalted above Atzilut. And the world of Beria has the level of Bina, namely Yeshsut. And the world of Yetzira has the level of ZA, and the world of Assiya has the level of Malchut.
The main difference between AK and ABYA is: that AK is from the first restriction, and ABYA are from the second restriction
And Atzilut is above the general Parsa, and BYA are below this Parsa

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14:4
items.html: Indeed, the main difference between these five worlds is by virtue of the two restrictions. For the world of Adam Kadmon is from the first restriction, in which the line of the light of Ein Sof shines in it down to the point of this world. And its first nine Sefirot are clean of any screen and restriction. This is not so with the four worlds ABYA, which are from the second restriction, in which from the Bina downward of every one of their degrees, the restriction of Malchut is already mixed in, by virtue of the ascent of Malchut to the Bina of every degree, as above. And the world of Atzilut, although it is from the second restriction, is nevertheless clean of any screen and restriction, because it is found from the general Parsa upward, and therefore the line of the light of Ein Sof shines in it down to its conclusion, namely down to the Parsa, which is the secret of the place of the chest of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, as above. And the world of Beria is already found below the general Parsa, namely after the light of the line from Ein Sof has already stopped, and it has only the light of offspring from the light of the line. Nevertheless, since it stands in the place of half of Tifferet of Nekudot deSAG of AK, and Tifferet is considered the Bina of the Guf, since the KHB of the Guf are called HGT, it is therefore corrected for the illumination of Bina, which is Yeshsut. And the world of Yetzira, standing in the place of NHY of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, which is the aspect of ZA, is corrected to receive the illumination of ZA of Atzilut. And the world of Assiya, standing in the place of Malchut of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, is corrected to receive the illumination of Malchut of Atzilut.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14:5
items.html: According to this you should understand that in AK, before the second restriction was made, there was no actual screen except at the point of this world, where its legs conclude. And all the screens mentioned in AK that are above the point of this world are only actions of this screen. And it is known that the coarseness of the screen cannot rise above the place of its existence even a little. So that only the effects of the screen alone rise above the place of its existence, but they are entirely without coarseness. Therefore there is no coarseness or screens at all in AK, although its screen is the coarsest of all the worlds, being phase four, as is known. For this coarseness begins to act only from the conclusion of its legs downward, which is only at the point of this world.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section III, Histaklut Penimit 14:6
items.html: Indeed, in the world of Atzilut the second restriction was made, and the Parsa between Atzilut and BYA was corrected, because of the ascent of Malchut of phase four from the point of this world, to the place of the chest of Partzuf Nekudot deSAG of AK, which stopped the light of Atzilut there, so that this new conclusion is called Parsa, as written in its place. And therefore the conclusion of the legs of all the Partzufim of Atzilut stopped at the place of this Parsa, since the light of Ein Sof no longer shines there, but only the light of offspring (as the ARI writes). And in this Parsa is found the screen of phase three, which concludes the legs of AA, because of the inclusion of phase four in the Parsa, and likewise the screens of the other Partzufim. And therefore from the Parsa downward the power of the screen already rules, since it stopped the upper light from Ein Sof. But from the Parsa upward there is no aspect of screen at all, but all the screens mentioned from the screen of the conclusion of the legs of Atzilut and upward are only actions rising from the power of the screen of the conclusion of the legs of the five Partzufim of Atzilut, which, although they receive all their illuminations through the screen of the conclusion of the legs, nevertheless they receive nothing of its coarseness, since the coarseness of the screen cannot rise above the place of its existence. Therefore there is no screen at all in any of the Partzufim of Atzilut.
